stories.why_ar: كثيرون يبحثون حيث يسهل البحث، لا حيث ضاع الشيء.
lines: One night, a neighbour found Juha on his knees under a street lamp.
"What are you doing?" he asked.
"I lost my key," said Juha. "Help me look for it."
They searched together for an hour and found nothing.
"Are you sure you lost it here?" the neighbour asked.
"No," said Juha. "I lost it inside my house."
"Then why are we looking in the street?"
Juha pointed at the lamp.
"Because the light is better here."
The neighbour went home thinking about his own life.
stories.moral_en: Search where the answer is, not where the searching is easy.
stories.moral_ar: ابحث حيث ضاع الأمر، لا حيث يسهل عليك البحث.

stories.title_en: Juha, His Son and the Donkey
stories.why_ar: من أراد أن يُرضي الناس كلّهم لم يُرضِ أحداً ولا نفسه.
lines: Juha and his son went to the market with their donkey.
Juha rode and the boy walked.
"Look at that man," people said. "He rides and his child walks!"
So Juha got down and put his son on the donkey.
"Look at that boy," others said. "His father walks in the sun!"
So they both rode.
"Poor animal," said the next people. "Two men on one small donkey!"
So they both got down and walked beside it.
"What fools," laughed the last people. "A donkey and nobody rides it."
Juha turned to his son and said, "Now you know."
stories.moral_en: Please everyone and you please no one.
stories.moral_ar: رضا الناس غاية لا تُدرَك، فاطلب الصواب ودَعْهم.

stories.why_ar: الجهد بلا توقّف للإصلاح يتحوّل إلى تعبٍ بلا نتيجة.
lines: A young woodcutter cut eighteen trees on his first day.
His boss was very happy with him.
The next day he worked harder and cut fifteen.
The third day he started earlier and cut ten.
Every day he tried more and cut less.
"When did you last sharpen your axe?" his boss asked.
"Sharpen it?" said the young man.
"I have had no time. I have been too busy cutting trees."
That evening he sat down with a stone and sharpened the blade.
The next day he cut twenty.
stories.moral_en: Sharpen the axe; working harder is not always working.
stories.moral_ar: من لم يجد وقتاً ليشحذ فأسه أفنى يومه في ضربٍ بلا أثر.

stories.why_ar: كلّ عائق يشكو منه الناس هو فرصة لمن يرفعه.
lines: A king put a large stone in the middle of the road one night.
Then he hid behind a tree and watched.
A rich merchant came and walked around it.
"Why does nobody clear this road?" he said, and went on.
Soldiers came and complained about the king.
Many people passed, and every one of them walked around the stone.
At last a poor farmer arrived with vegetables.
He put down his load and pushed the stone with his shoulder.
Under it was a small bag of gold and a note from the king.
"For the one who moves the stone."
stories.moral_en: Every obstacle carries a chance for the one who lifts it.
stories.moral_ar: تحت الحجر الذي يشكو منه الناس أجرُ من يزيحه.

stories.why_ar: غضبك ليس من الحادث، بل من الشخص الذي تتخيّله وراءه.
lines: A man was crossing a river in his small boat.
Another boat came fast out of the fog and hit him.
He stood up and shouted angrily at the other boat.
"Are you blind? Watch where you are going!"
Then the fog opened a little.
He saw that the other boat was empty.
It had come loose and the river had carried it.
There was nobody to shout at.
His anger left him at once, and he felt strange.
The boat was the same boat. Only the person had gone.
stories.moral_en: Most of our anger is aimed at a person we imagine.
stories.moral_ar: أكثر غضبنا موجَّه إلى شخصٍ نتخيّله في القارب الفارغ.

stories.why_ar: الألم لا يتغيّر، لكنّ الإناء الذي تضعه فيه يتغيّر.
lines: A student came to his teacher full of sadness.
The teacher asked him to put a handful of salt in a glass of water.
"Drink it," he said.
The young man drank and made a face. "It is bitter."
Then they walked to a lake.
The teacher told him to throw another handful of salt into it.
"Now drink from the lake."
The student drank and the water was sweet.
"The salt was the same," said the teacher.
"The pain in your life is the salt. You decide how big the water is."
stories.moral_en: The same pain tastes different in a larger life.
stories.moral_ar: المِلح واحد، والفرق في سعة الإناء.

stories.why_ar: الأمان الذي يمنعك من النموّ ليس أماناً.
lines: Two seeds lay side by side in the spring earth.
The first said, "I want to grow. I will send my roots down."
"I will push my stem up and open my leaves to the sun."
And it did.
The second said, "It is dark down here, but it is safe."
"If I send my roots down, who knows what I will meet?"
"If I push up, someone may step on me."
"I will wait until it is safer."
And it waited.
A few days later a hen came, scratched the ground, and ate it.
stories.moral_en: Waiting for safety is its own risk.
stories.moral_ar: من انتظر الأمان في مكانه أكله الانتظار.

stories.why_ar: من جاء ممتلئاً برأيه لم يبقَ فيه موضع للتعلّم.
lines: A professor visited a quiet old teacher to learn from him.
From the first minute, he talked about his own ideas.
The teacher listened and began to pour tea into his guest's cup.
The cup filled up.
The teacher kept pouring.
Tea ran over the table and onto the floor.
"Stop!" said the professor. "It is full. No more will go in."
The teacher put down the pot.
"Like this cup," he said, "you are full of your own opinions."
"How can I show you anything until you empty your cup?"
stories.moral_en: Empty your cup before you ask to be filled.
stories.moral_ar: لا يدخل العلمُ قلباً ملأه صاحبه برأيه.

stories.why_ar: الخطة التي لا تبدأ اليوم ليست خطة.
lines: Two brothers wanted to buy a fishing boat.
The first made a plan for ten years.
He drew the boat, he counted the money, and he talked about it every night.
The second bought one small net.
He went to the water before sunrise and came back with three fish.
He sold them and bought a second net.
The first brother was still drawing.
After two years the second brother had a boat.
"You were lucky," said his brother.
"Maybe," he said. "But I was also wet every morning."
stories.moral_en: A small start beats a perfect plan.
stories.moral_ar: بدايةٌ صغيرة اليوم خيرٌ من خطّةٍ كاملة غداً.

stories.why_ar: الجواب الذي تبحث عنه في يدك أنت.
lines: A clever boy wanted to prove that the village wise woman knew nothing.
He caught a small bird and held it behind his back.
"I will ask her if the bird is alive or dead," he told his friends.
"If she says alive, I will close my hand."
"If she says dead, I will open it and let it fly."
He stood in front of her and asked his question.
The old woman looked at him for a long moment.
She did not look at his hands.
"My son," she said, "the answer is in your hands."
The boy opened his hand and the bird flew up into the sky.
stories.moral_en: The answer is in your hands.
stories.moral_ar: ما تسأل عنه ليس عند غيرك، بل في يدك.
